hook.line: When you have a plan and need people to agree, a proposal sounds more serious than "what if we...". It is the voice of someone chairing a meeting.
hook.es: Les propongo que nos reunamos el lunes.
hook.en: I suggest that we meet on Monday. (to a group)

examples.en: I suggest that we meet on Monday. (to a group)

examples.en: I suggest going to the cinema on Saturday. (to a friend)
I suggest that we cook together. (to a friend)

rule:
*Proponer* is "to propose". Put the person first (*te*, *le*, *les*), then *propongo*.

There are two ways to finish:

*Te propongo ir al cine.* Use the plain infinitive when the plan is just you and them.

*Te propongo que vayamos al cine.* Use *que* plus the "asking" ending when you want to name who does it. *Vamos* becomes *vayamos*, *nos reunimos* becomes *nos reunamos*.

A proposal tries to move people, so it works like *te recomiendo que*. The casual *¿qué tal si vamos?* is lighter and uses the normal verb.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after a verb of influence, the same family as *recomendar* and *pedir*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *vamos* or *vayamos* and type the whole sentence: *Te propongo que ___ al cine el sábado.*
yourTurn.answer: Te propongo que vayamos al cine el sábado.
yourTurn.why: After *te propongo que*, the verb takes the "asking" form: *vayamos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a group: I suggest that we meet on Monday.
yourTurn.answer: Les propongo que nos reunamos el lunes.
accept: Yo les propongo que nos reunamos el lunes.
yourTurn.why: *Les* is the group, and *nos reunamos* is the changed form of *nos reunimos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I suggest going to the cinema on Saturday.
yourTurn.answer: Te propongo ir al cine el sábado.
accept: Yo te propongo ir al cine el sábado.
yourTurn.why: When the plan is shared, the plain infinitive is enough.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I suggest that we cook together.
accept: Yo te propongo que cocinemos juntos.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, formal: I suggest that you read the contract first.
yourTurn.answer: Le propongo que lea el contrato primero.
accept: Le propongo que primero lea el contrato.
Yo le propongo que lea el contrato primero.
yourTurn.why: *Le* is the formal *usted*, and *lea* is the changed form of *lee*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Vale suggests that we open earlier.
yourTurn.answer: Vale propone que abramos más temprano.
yourTurn.why: *Propone* for Vale, then *que* and *abramos*, the changed form of *abrimos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: What do you suggest that we do?

pitfalls.wrong: Te propongo que vamos al cine.
pitfalls.right: Te propongo que vayamos al cine.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A proposal tries to move people, so the verb after *que* takes the "asking" ending.

pitfalls.wrong: Te propongo a ir al cine.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Proponer* takes the infinitive directly, with no *a*.

pitfalls.right: Les propongo que nos reunamos el lunes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Name who you are proposing to with *te*, *le* or *les*.

personal: Propose a plan to a friend for this weekend, starting with *Te propongo que* or *Te propongo*.
